clues.title: Road line: Yellow Outer Lines
text: In South Africa, most paved roads have **single yellow outer lines** and **white center lines**. This can be used to differentiate from Australia which has only **white lines** and never single yellow lines.
**REMEMBER:**
The Middle East can also have single yellow outer lines, so use driving side to tell them apart (South Africa drives left)
Botswana, Eswatini and Lesotho also use single yellow outer lines (but they usually have a white car)

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Infrastructure - Three Stripes
text: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of reflective tape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Infrastructure - Durban Lamp
text: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this bump on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Infrastructure - Dodgy Adverts
text: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with dodgy adverts for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - R360 North of Bokspits
text: The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.
NOTE: Asphalt with a reddish tint can be found on other roads and the southern part of the R360. However, the landscape north of Bokspits looks predominantly like this.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Cape Town Mountains
text: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - George Mountains
text: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.
